title: Applied ML Evals: end-to-end onboarding, quantization, and regression triage playbook
author: Priya Natarajan
content:
Purpose and scope

This playbook describes our end-to-end applied ML evaluation process for onboarding models into Redwood Inference, maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, applying quantization profiles safely, and operating a regression triage process that keeps production quality within our SLA and guardrails. It consolidates guidance from the eval harness, prompt set owners, quantization team, and regression triage responders. Use this doc when:

- Onboarding a new model version for serving.
- Creating or curating prompt sets and benchmark suites.
- Applying quantization profiles to reduce cost.
- Investigating and triaging model quality regressions.

High-level responsibilities

- Model owner: coordinates onboarding, defines target tasks, and owns final accept/reject decisions.
- Eval engineers: implement eval harness test configs, run automated suites, and interpret metrics.
- Quantization team: creates and verifies quantization profiles and safety limits.
- Observability/Platform: ensures telemetry, traces, and rollout controls are present.
- Regression triage on-call: executes triage playbooks and coordinates rollbacks or mitigations.

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)

1) Pre-onboard (owner + eval engineers)
   - Define target tasks and success criteria (task list, acceptance thresholds).
   - Register model in model catalog with metadata: architecture, training data summary, tokenization, expected seq lengths, and dependencies.
   - Identify representative prompt sets and baseline model for comparison.

2) Eval harness integration
   - Add model to eval harness config (yaml): dataset list, sampling seeds, generation params (max_tokens, temperature, top_p), evaluation metrics.
   - Run unit verification: tokenization parity, deterministic generation tests, and simple accuracy checks on small datasets.
   - Run full automated suite: all prompt sets and benchmarks described below. Capture outputs and artifacts in eval run.

3) Quantization validation (if applicable)
   - Apply baseline 16-bit or FP32 verification first.
   - Create quantization profile candidate (8-bit/4-bit) with expected performance gains and known limitations.
   - Run the targeted quantization regression suite (see 'Quantization regression tests' section).
   - If regressions exceed allowable deltas, escalate to quantization team for profile tuning.

4) Canary rollout & quality monitoring
   - Deploy as canary traffic routing (5% initial) with A/B comparison to baseline.
   - Monitor prompt-level metrics, token-level distributions, latency, cost, and safety signals for 24-72 hours.
   - Escalate or rollback on breach of thresholds (see SLOs/thresholds table).

Eval harness: structure and conventions

- Test config format: yaml with top-level keys: datasets, generation_params, metrics, artifacts, tags. Keep configs under eval-configs/<model>/<release>.
- Determinism: for regression-sensitive suites, fix seeds and remove temperature sampling. For robustness and diversity suites, use controlled stochastic sampling and aggregate over multiple seeds.
- Artifacts: store full model responses, embeddings, logits (when enabled), and evaluation outputs in the eval artifact store. Link run IDs in PRs and onboarding tickets.

Prompt sets and benchmarks: guidance

- Prompt set taxonomy:
  - Functional examples: typical product prompts that customers use.
  - Edge cases: adversarial, ambiguous, and long-sequence prompts.
  - Safety/Security: prompts designed to probe policy violations and hallucination risk.
  - Performance stress: long-context and burst workloads to surface latency and memory issues.

- Versioning: store prompt sets with semantic version tags. Maintain a canonical manifest file listing prompt set id, owner, intended tasks, and last-run baseline.

- Benchmark types and metrics:
  - Accuracy/regression metrics: exact match, F1, BLEU, ROUGE where applicable.
  - Semantic similarity: embedding-based similarity with threshold gates.
  - Safety: policy score and human-in-the-loop labels.
  - Latency/cost: p50/p95 token latencies and cost-per-1k-tokens.
  - Calibration: expected token entropy and confidence distributions.

Quantization profiles: lifecycle and checks

- Profile stages: draft -> candidate -> verified -> recommended. Each profile contains: quantization method, per-layer exceptions, calibration dataset, and expected perf gains.
- Guardrails: a quantization profile must define max-allowed regression deltas per metric and a set of 'must-pass' tests for safety-critical prompt sets.

Quantization regression tests (minimum suite)

- Functional parity suite: representative production prompts, must have delta <= 1.5% absolute on primary metric.
- Safety suite: policy-sensitive prompts, must pass at same policy verdicts or be escalated.
- Semantic similarity: average embedding similarity >= 0.95 vs baseline on core datasets.
- Calibration suite: verify logits distribution shifts do not break downstream confidence thresholds.

Regression triage playbook (on-detect)

Detection triggers:
- Automated alert: metric drift > configured delta (see thresholds table).
- Customer report: high-severity ticket with reproducible failing prompt.
- Canary breach: canary rollout indicates reduced quality.

Immediate steps (first 30 minutes):
1) Acknowledge alert and create triage incident in the tracking system with tag 'model-regression'.
2) Capture failing prompt(s), model version, eval run id, and system metadata (latency, region, config).
3) Reproduce locally using eval harness deterministic config.

Triage and resolution (30 minutes to 8 hours):
1) Classify regression: data drift, model change, quantization effect, serving bug, or infrastructure (latency/memory).
2) If reproducible and caused by a recent model release or quantization change, rollback canary to baseline and escalate to model owner.
3) If not reproducible, expand sampling and run full benchmark suite. Request human review for safety cases.
4) Where possible apply temporary mitigations: route to baseline model, increase temperature constraints, or enable prefix caching to avoid cold-start hallucinations.

Root cause and postmortem (>8 hours):
- Assign RCA owner and set 5-day SL for a written postmortem if customer-visible impact. Include: timeline, reproducer, metrics before/after, remediation, and preventive actions.

SLOs, thresholds, and alerting matrix

- Primary metric delta allowed for onboarding: accuracy-based metrics <= 2% absolute vs baseline.
- Quantization allowed delta: functional metrics <= 1.5% absolute; embedding similarity >= 0.95.
- Canary thresholds: p50 latency change <= 15%; p95 latency change <= 25%; error rate increase <= 0.1% absolute.
- Safety policy: no new policy violations accepted in canary. Any new violation triggers immediate rollback.

Example thresholds table (text representation)

Metric | Baseline | Allowed delta | Alert level
- Accuracy (primary) | baseline | <= 2% abs | critical
- Embedding sim (mean) | baseline | >= 0.95 | high
- p95 latency | baseline | <= +25% | warning
- Safety policy verdicts | baseline | no new violations | critical

Telemetry and dashboards

- Mandatory telemetry emitted during onboarding/canary: run_id, model_version, quant_profile, prompt_set_id, latency_ms, tokens, error_flags, safety_scores.
- Dashboards: per-model-per-route dashboards visualizing the prompt-set breakdown, metric deltas, and per-prompt histograms. Use the eval run id for traceability.

Human-in-the-loop review process

- For safety and high-visibility customers, route failing cases to the human review queue. Label each case with severity and suggested actions. Reviews must complete within 24 hours during business days.

CLI and example commands (eval harness)

- Run a deterministic unit suite:
  ./eval_harness run --model my-model:2026-05-30 --config configs/functional-suite.yaml --seed 42 --output ./artifacts/run-123

- Run quantization candidate suite:
  ./eval_harness run --model my-model:2026-05-30 --config configs/quantization-regression.yaml --quant-profile q8_candidate --output ./artifacts/q-run-456

Documentation and artifacts

- Every onboarding must include: eval run link, quant profile definition (if used), prompt-set manifest, canary routing config, and rollback plan. Store artifacts in the eval artifact store and link to the onboarding ticket.

Related pages and references

- See the eval harness standards and eval-config examples for config templates. See quantization profiles best practices for technical knobs and per-layer overrides. See regression triage playbook for incident templates and on-call rotations.

Appendix: example eval-config (yaml-style example)

- datasets: [functional-v1, safety-v2, long-context-stress]
- generation_params: {max_tokens: 256, temperature: 0.0, top_p: 0.95}
- metrics: [accuracy_primary, embedding_similarity, policy_score, latency_p95]
- artifacts: [responses, embeddings, logits]

Notes and next steps

- Update this playbook when introducing new quantization methods or when adding new high-impact prompt sets. Annual review required by applied-ml leadership.

Contact and ownership

- Playbook owner: Priya Natarajan (applied-ml)
- Quantization lead: Marco Diaz
- Eval harness lead: Asha Li

This document is intended to be a single source of truth for cross-functional teams during model onboarding, quantization profiling, and regression triage. Keep links to run artifacts and tickets current to preserve traceability.
